mainTopic: How the rule that Ammonite and Moabite women are permitted was confirmed and grounded, how it shaped דוד's royal line, and whether the daughter of an Ammonite convert may marry a כהן.
overview: דואג raises hard questions that nearly get דוד, a descendant of רות the Moabite, declared unfit to marry into the Jewish people. רבא explains that עמשא's father יתר drew his sword and declared a tradition from שמואל's court: an Ammonite or Moabite man is banned, but not a woman. The גמרא asks how יתר could be believed when the ruling touched his own family, and answers that שמואל's court was still alive to confirm it. It then explains why women were not expected to go out and greet the Jews, using two פסוקים, and links the source of the rule to a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. רבא gives three דרשות showing how this rule saved דוד's royal line, through רות and נעמה. Then עולא quotes רבי יוחנן that the daughter of an Ammonite convert may marry a כהן, and רבא בר עולא challenges this by trying to derive the opposite from a כהן גדול who married a widow and from a חלל. The ruling turns out to be about an Ammonite who married a Jewish-born woman. רבין reports that רבי יוחנן says the daughter is fit and ריש לקיש says she is disqualified, and רבי יוחנן's reason comes on the next amud.

steps.title: דואג's objections silence everyone
steps.stepSummary: דואג raises all his objections, no one can answer, and he wants to publicly declare דוד unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: דואג asked them all these difficult questions, and they were silent. He wanted to make a public announcement about him (דוד).
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: דואג's questions leave the scholars with no answer, and he is ready to announce that דוד is disqualified. This sets up the dramatic answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד descends from רות the Moabite woman. If the rule of עמוני ולא עמונית cannot be defended, דוד would be barred from marrying into the Jewish people. The silence shows how serious דואג's challenge was.

phrases.english: Doeg raised against them
all these difficulties,
and they were silent.
He wanted to make a proclamation about him.
phrases.notes: "Him" is דוד. דואג wanted to announce that דוד may not marry into the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַקְשִׁי לְהוּ דּוֹאֵג כֹּל הָנֵי קוּשְׁיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous עמוד about דוד's lineage.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule עמוני ולא עמונית, and with it דוד's status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דואג's objections seemed to show that women should also be included in the ban, so דוד, a descendant of רות, would be disqualified.

steps.title: עמשא's father יתר declares the tradition from שמואל's court
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים call עמשא's father both 'Israelite' and 'Yishmaelite'. רבא explains that he drew his sword like a Yishmaelite and declared the tradition: an Ammonite or Moabite man is forbidden, not a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away: 'And עמשא was the son of a man named יתרא the Israelite, who came to אביגל daughter of נחש.' Yet another פסוק says 'יתר the Yishmaelite.' רבא said: this teaches that he girded his sword like a Yishmaelite and said: Whoever does not accept this הלכה will be stabbed by the sword. This is what I received from the court of שמואל of Ramah: an Ammonite man, not an Ammonite woman; a Moabite man, not a Moabite woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer to דואג comes immediately, in a dramatic way. רבא uses two פסוקים that describe the same person differently to show that עמשא's father forcefully declared the tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים seem to contradict each other: is he an Israelite or a Yishmaelite? רבא explains that he was a real Israelite but acted 'like a Yishmaelite' by drawing his sword to defend the הלכה. He does not argue with דואג's logic. He brings a received tradition from שמואל's court.

keyTerms.meaning: will be stabbed by the sword
I have received as a tradition
an Ammonite man, not an Ammonite woman

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source showing that the rule permitting Moabite women was a known tradition. That rule is what makes דוד's lineage, through רות, kosher.

phrases.english: Immediately
"And Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Yisra

phrases.aramaic: הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי אֲשֶׁר בָּא אֶל אֲבִיגַל בַּת נָחָשׁ״,
phrases.english: the Israelite, who came to Avigal daughter of Nachash,"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 17:25

phrases.english: and it is written: "Yeser the Yishmaelite."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:17

phrases.english: Rava said: This teaches
that he girded his sword like a Yishmaelite,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ הֲלָכָה זוֹ
phrases.english: and said: Whoever does not accept this halacha
will be stabbed with the sword.
So have I received
from the court of Shmuel of Ramah:
"An Ammonite" man, and not an Ammonite woman.
"A Moabite" man, and not a Moabite woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the crisis דואג created.
steps.terutzMaskana: A tradition from שמואל's court says Ammonite and Moabite women are permitted.

steps.title: Can יתר be believed about his own family?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges יתר's testimony. רב taught that a scholar who reports a ruling only once it affects him is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is he believed? But didn't רבי אבא say in the name of רב: any תלמיד חכם who comes and states a הלכה, if he said it before the case came up, we listen to him; if not, we don't listen to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks how עמשא's tradition could be accepted at all, given a rule about scholars reporting rulings that matter to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יתר was married to אביגיל, the daughter of ישי, so the ruling affected his own wife and children. רב's rule says a scholar who reports a tradition only once the case touches him may be biased. So יתר should not have been trusted.
steps.confusionAlert: רב's rule does not say the scholar is a liar. It only says we cannot rely on him when he reports the ruling after it became personally relevant.

phrases.english: And is he trusted?
phrases.notes: "He" is יתר, who was married to ישי's daughter אביגיל, so this ruling touched his own family.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abba say that Rav said:
Any Torah scholar
who comes and states a halachic ruling,
if he said it before the case arose,
we listen to him,
and if not, we do not listen to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מְהֵימַן? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the testimony in step 2 can be accepted.
steps.kashyaTarget: יתר's reliability as a witness to the tradition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב's rule, a ruling first reported when it becomes personally relevant is not accepted.

steps.title: שמואל's court was still alive
steps.stepSummary: This case is different because שמואל and his court were alive and could confirm the tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because שמואל and his court were still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: יתר's claim could easily be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule worries that a scholar might invent or bend a tradition. Here the original source, שמואל's court, was still alive. No one would make a claim that could be disproved so easily.

phrases.english: Here it is different,
since Shmuel and his court were alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא, דְּהָא שְׁמוּאֵל וּבֵית דִּינוֹ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יתר is an interested party, so he should not be believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: His testimony could be verified directly, so it is accepted.

steps.title: Doeg's question still needs an answer
steps.stepSummary: Even with the tradition accepted, the logical difficulty דואג raised is still unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a tradition was given, but no one has yet explained the reasoning behind דואג's question. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition tells us what the הלכה is, but not how it fits the פסוק's reason, 'they did not greet you with bread and water'. Why shouldn't the women have gone out to greet the Jewish women? Steps 6 and 7 answer this.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult!
phrases.notes: "It" is דואג's question, which so far was answered only by tradition and not by reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side question about עמשא to דואג's original question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ban exists because they did not greet the Jews, women should have greeted Jewish women, so they should be banned too.

steps.title: Babylonian answer: a princess's honor is inside
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they explained, using a פסוק in תהלים, that a woman's dignity is to stay inside, so women were not expected to go out to greet anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here (in בבל) they explained: 'All the honor of the king's daughter is within.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer to דואג's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is based on failing to go out and greet. Women were never expected to go out, so they were not at fault. That is why the ban applies only to men.

keyTerms.meaning: all the honor of a king's daughter is within

phrases.english: Here they explained:
phrases.notes: "Here" means in בבל, where the גמרא was composed.

phrases.english: "All the honor of the king's daughter is within."
phrases.notes: תהלים 45:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Women should have greeted Jewish women.
steps.terutzMaskana: Women's dignity is to stay inside, so they were not expected to go out.

steps.title: Answer from ארץ ישראל: שרה was in the tent
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל, or רבי יצחק, brought a פסוק about שרה being in the tent to show the same idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they say, and some say it was רבי יצחק: the פסוק says, 'And they said to him: Where is שרה your wife?' (and he said: in the tent).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second source for the same answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels asked where שרה was, and the answer was that she was in the tent. This is praised as proper conduct for a woman. The conclusion is the same as in step 6, but from a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: in the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: In the West they say,
and some say it was Rabbi Yitzchak:
The verse says:
"And they said to him: Where is Sarah your wife? etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:9. The "etc." points to the rest of the פסוק: "Behold, in the tent."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second source for the answer in step 6.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is praiseworthy for a woman to stay home, so women were not expected to greet.

steps.title: A dispute between תנאים about the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares this to a dispute between תנאים. רבי יהודה learns the rule from the masculine words עמוני and מואבי, while רבי שמעון learns it from the reason given: it is a man's way to go out and greet.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: 'An Ammonite', not an Ammonite woman; 'a Moabite', not a Moabite woman. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says: 'Because they did not greet you with bread and water': it is the way of a man to go out and greet, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two ways of grounding the rule match an earlier dispute between תנאים: learning it from the wording 'עמוני' (as in the tradition יתר declared in step 2), or from the reason that women do not go out to greet (as in steps 6-7).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learns the rule from the wording itself: the פסוק says the masculine 'עמוני', not 'עמונית'. רבי שמעון learns it from the reason the Torah gives: greeting travelers is a man's role, so women were never at fault. Both allow Moabite women, but they disagree about the source.

keyTerms.meaning: it is the way of a man

steps.whatToRemember: Moabite and Ammonite women are permitted to marry into the Jewish people. רבי יהודה learns this from the masculine wording, and רבי שמעון from the reason: women do not go out to greet. This is why דוד's lineage through רות is valid.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון agree on the הלכה. They disagree only about which part of the פסוק teaches it.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute between Tannaim:
"An Ammonite" man, and not an Ammonite woman;
"a Moabite" man, and not a Moabite woman.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Shimon says:
"Because they did not come out to meet you
with bread and with water"
phrases.notes: דברים 23:5

phrases.english: it is the way of a man to go out to meet, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." means: but it is not the way of a woman, so women are not included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the discussion about the reason behind the rule to an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה derives the permission for women from the masculine wording. רבי שמעון derives it from the reason that only men go out to greet.

steps.title: דוד thanks ה׳ for loosening his two bands
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the פסוק "פתחת למוסרי". דוד thanks ה׳ for freeing him from two 'bands': רות the Moabite and נעמה the Ammonite.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק "You have loosened my bands" mean? דוד said to ה׳: Master of the world, there were two bands tied on me, and You loosened them. They are רות the Moabite and נעמה the Ammonite.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a דרשה showing that דוד himself was grateful for the rule that Moabite and Ammonite women are allowed to marry into the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'bands' are two possible problems in דוד's family line. If women had been included in the ban, רות and נעמה, and everyone descended from them, could not have married into the Jewish people. Because the ban covers only men, these 'bands' were opened.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded; taught a lesson drawn from a פסוק
What is the meaning of what is written
Bands or straps, here meaning things that tied him down

phrases.english: Rava expounded: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"You have loosened my bands"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:16

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: David said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
two bands that were on me, You loosened them:
Ruth the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule from Step 8 that only male Moabites and Ammonites are banned, and shows how much it meant for דוד's family.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד praised ה׳ because the women-are-permitted rule kept רות and נעמה, and so his royal line, acceptable.

steps.title: "Upon us" includes רחבעם on דוד's lap
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the plural word "אלינו" that דוד was talking about himself and also about his grandson רחבעם, who was sitting on his lap.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק "Many things have You done, ה׳ my God, Your wonders and Your thoughts are upon us" mean? It does not say "upon me". It says "upon us". This teaches that רחבעם was sitting on דוד's lap, and דוד told him: These two פסוקים were said about me and about you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second דרשה. He reads the plural "us" as including רחבעם, whose mother was the Ammonite נעמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra point comes from one word: "אלינו" (us) instead of "אלי" (me). דוד was helped through רות, and רחבעם was helped through נעמה. Both of them gained from the same rule.

phrases.english: Rava expounded: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Many things have You done, O Lord my God,
Your wonders and Your thoughts are upon us"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 40:6

phrases.english: "Upon me" is not stated, but rather "upon us";
this teaches that Rehoboam was
sitting on the lap of David,
and he said to him: About me and about you
these two verses were stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק and extends the gratitude from דוד alone to his grandson רחבעם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plural "אלינו" shows that דוד was speaking for both himself and רחבעם.

steps.title: דוד's coming was already written in the story of לוט's daughters
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains "in the scroll of a book it is written about me". דוד's existence was hinted at long before, through the shared word "found" in the story of לוט's daughters and in a פסוק about דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק "Then I said: Here I have come; in the scroll of a book it is written about me" mean? דוד said: I thought I had only now come into the world. I did not know that it was already written about me in a book. There, about לוט's daughters, it says "that are found". Here, about דוד, it says "I have found דוד My servant; with My holy oil I anointed him".
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third דרשה. He uses the matching word "found" to link דוד to the daughters of לוט, who were the mothers of עמון and מואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "הנמצאות" (that are found) in the story of לוט is matched with "מצאתי" (I have found) in the פסוק about דוד. The lesson is that דוד was the 'find' that came out of לוט's daughters. His royal line was planned long before he was born.
steps.confusionAlert: "There" is not a place mentioned earlier on the daf. It points to a פסוק in בראשית about לוט's daughters, which the גמרא quotes with just one word.

phrases.english: Rava expounded: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Then I said: Behold, I have come;
in the scroll of a book it is written about me"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 40:8

phrases.english: David said: I said, "I have come only now,"

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יָדַעְתִּי שֶׁ״בִּמְגִילַּת סֵפֶר כָּתוּב עָלָי״.
phrases.english: and I did not know that "in the scroll of a book it is written about me."
There it is written: "that are found,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 19:15, about the daughters of לוט.

phrases.english: and here it is written:
"I have found David, My servant;
with My holy oil I have anointed him."
phrases.notes: תהלים 89:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last of רבא's teachings. It traces דוד's line all the way back to the mothers of עמון and מואב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shared word links לוט's daughters to דוד, showing that דוד's line was hinted at from long ago.
steps.whatToRemember: All three of רבא's teachings show the same thing: the rule allowing Moabite and Ammonite women is what made דוד's royal family possible.

steps.title: The daughter of an Ammonite convert may marry a כהן
steps.stepSummary: עולא, quoting רבי יוחנן, rules that the daughter of a man who converted from עמון may marry into כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The daughter of an Ammonite convert is allowed to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new legal point. Not only may an Ammonite convert's daughter marry a regular Jew, she may even marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father is an Ammonite convert, who himself may not marry into the Jewish people. Even so, רבי יוחנן says his daughter is fully acceptable, even for a כהן. This sets up the next question about which תנא this ruling follows.

phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The daughter of an Ammonite convert
is fit for the priesthood.
phrases.notes: He means she may marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the aggadic teachings back to practical הלכה about Ammonite descendants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter of an Ammonite convert is permitted to marry a כהן.

steps.title: Whose opinion does this follow?
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר עולא asks whose view the ruling follows. According to רבי יהודה it seems wrong, and according to רבי יוסי it seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר עולא said to עולא: Whose opinion is this? If it follows רבי יהודה, he said that the daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male חלל, so she may not marry a כהן. If it follows רבי יוסי, it is obvious, because he said that even when a convert marries a convert, their daughter may marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר עולא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling with a two-sided question. Neither opinion seems to make the ruling both correct and worth saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה disqualifies any convert's daughter from marrying a כהן, so he would not permit an Ammonite convert's daughter. רבי יוסי permits even a daughter whose father and mother were both converts, so why would רבי יוחנן need to say it? This sets up the answer that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A person born from a forbidden union of a כהן, who loses כהונה status

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר עוּלָּא לְעוּלָּא: כְּמַאן?
phrases.english: Rava bar Ulla said to Ulla: In accordance with whom?
If it is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, didn't he say:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת גֵּר זָכָר — כְּבַת חָלָל זָכָר!
phrases.english: The daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male ḥalal!
And if in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, it is obvious,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר: אַף גֵּר שֶׁנָּשָׂא גִּיּוֹרֶת —
phrases.english: for he said: Even a male convert who married a female convert,
his daughter is fit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר עוּלָּא לְעוּלָּא: כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 12 by trying to match it to a known תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the daughter of an Ammonite convert may marry a כהן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma. Under רבי יהודה the ruling is wrong, since any convert's daughter is disqualified. Under רבי יוסי the ruling is unnecessary, since even a daughter of two converts is permitted.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי only meant converts who may enter the קהל, but where would he get that?
steps.stepSummary: The challenge blocks a possible defense. Perhaps רבי יוסי allowed only the daughters of converts who may marry into the Jewish people, and not an עמוני. If so, what is his source for that distinction?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that רבי יוסי only meant converts who are fit to enter the קהל, but this convert from עמון, who is not fit to enter the קהל, is not included, then from where would he learn that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines a way to save the ruling of עולא, and then questions it. It asks what source רבי יוסי would have for treating a convert from עמון differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, the ruling seemed too obvious according to רבי יוסי. One way out is to say that רבי יוסי only permitted converts who are allowed to marry into the קהל. Then the ruling about an עמוני would be a real new teaching. But that distinction needs a source, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (it introduces a possible answer)
The congregation, meaning marrying into the Jewish people
From where does he know this?

phrases.english: And if you would say
[he spoke only] about those who are fit to enter the congregation
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוסי's ruling that a convert's daughter may marry a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַאי דְּאֵין רָאוּי לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל — לָא,
phrases.english: but this one, who is not fit to enter the congregation, no
from where would he learn this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, בְּהָנָךְ דִּרְאוּיִן לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge of step 13 by closing off a possible way to defend the ruling according to רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יוסי limited his permission to converts who may enter the קהל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A distinction like this needs a source, and none is obvious.

steps.title: He could learn it from a כהן גדול who married a widow
steps.stepSummary: The proposed source is a כהן גדול who married an אלמנה. The man was forbidden to make that marriage, and his daughter is disqualified from כהונה. In the same way, an עמוני convert is forbidden to marry a Jewish woman, so his daughter would be disqualified too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from a כהן גדול who married a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible source for treating an עמוני convert's daughter as unfit for כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both men are forbidden to make the marriage they made. Because the daughter of a כהן גדול and an אלמנה is disqualified, the same rule could apply to the daughter of a man who may not enter the קהל.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow, whom a כהן גדול may not marry

phrases.english: He learns it from a High Priest [who married] a widow.
phrases.notes: A כהן גדול may not marry a widow (ויקרא 21:14), and a daughter from that marriage may not marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'מנא ליה' from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for treating the daughter of an עמוני convert as disqualified.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison to a כהן גדול who married an אלמנה.

steps.title: But the כהן גדול committed a sin when he married her
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is attacked. When a כהן גדול marries an אלמנה, the union itself is a sin. An עמוני convert can marry a female עמונית convert with no sin at all, so the two cases are not alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a כהן גדול with a widow? That case is different, because his union with her is a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a weakness in the comparison to the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter may be disqualified only because she came from a forbidden act. An עמוני convert's daughter can come from a fully permitted marriage. So the כהן גדול case cannot teach us about the עמוני on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: What about this case? (a formula that points out a difference)

phrases.english: What about a High Priest with a widow?
That case is different, because his union is a sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה שֶׁכֵּן בִּיאָתוֹ בַּעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source proposed in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of an עמוני convert to a כהן גדול with an אלמנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן גדול case has a sinful union, which the עמוני case does not have to have.

steps.title: A חלל proves that a sinful union is not needed
steps.stepSummary: A חלל can marry a regular Jewish woman with no sin, and his daughter is still disqualified from כהונה. So a sinful union is not what causes the daughter to be disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let a חלל prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the attack with a different case, a חלל, where there is no sinful union and the daughter is still disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes away the difference raised in step 16. If a daughter can be disqualified without any forbidden act, the עמוני convert's daughter could be disqualified too.

keyTerms.meaning: A man born from a union forbidden to כהנים, who loses the status of כהונה
Let it prove (a case that shows a point does not matter)

phrases.english: Let a חלל prove it!
phrases.notes: A חלל may marry a regular Jewish woman, yet his daughter still may not marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the source from the attack in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A counter-example that removes the difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The daughter is disqualified only when her father's union was a sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חלל shows that a daughter can be disqualified even when the union was permitted.

steps.title: But a חלל himself was born from a sin
steps.stepSummary: The חלל case is also attacked. The חלל himself came from a forbidden union, so it makes sense that his flaw passes to his children. An עמוני convert was not born from a forbidden union.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a חלל? That case is different, because he himself was formed through a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a different weakness in the חלל case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a חלל, the flaw is already in the father from his birth, so the daughter may simply inherit it. An עמוני convert has no such flaw from birth, so the חלל cannot teach us about him alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Formation, meaning how a person came into being

phrases.english: What about a חלל?
That case is different, because he was formed through a sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the חלל case from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using a חלל to learn about an עמוני convert.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חלל was born from a sin, but an עמוני convert was not.

steps.title: The כהן גדול proves it again, and the proof goes in a circle
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול was not born from a sin, yet his daughter from an אלמנה is disqualified. This answers the attack on the חלל. Now each case answers the weakness of the other, so the argument has come back to where it began.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the כהן גדול prove it. And the reasoning has come back around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the כהן גדול case again. It then notes that the argument has gone in a full circle, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has its own weakness, but the other case answers it. The כהן גדול was born without a sin, and the חלל's union was permitted. 'וחזר הדין' signals that neither case works alone, so the גמרא is getting ready to learn from what the two cases share.

keyTerms.meaning: And the reasoning has come back around (the cases answer each other)

steps.confusionAlert: 'וחזר הדין' does not mean the proof failed. It means each case covers the other's weakness, so the גמרא will next look at what the two cases have in common.

phrases.english: Let the High Priest prove it.
And the reasoning has come back around:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack in step 18 and closes the circle that began in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A counter-example that brings back the first case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A daughter is disqualified only if her father was born from a sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן גדול was not born from a sin, yet his daughter is disqualified. Now the two cases support each other.

steps.title: Combining the two sources: the common denominator
steps.stepSummary: Neither the כהן גדול case nor the חלל case works alone, but together they share a common feature. Each man is not like the majority of the קהל, and each one's daughter is disqualified. So the עמוני convert, who is also not like the majority of the קהל, should have a disqualified daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case is not like that case, and that case is not like this case. What they share is that he is not like most of the קהל, and his daughter is disqualified. So too here, he is not like most of the קהל, so his daughter is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the two sources that each failed alone and joins them into one proof, using what they have in common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source had its own weak point, and the other source covered it. Since neither weak point is the real reason, the גמרא looks for the feature both cases share: the man stands apart from the rest of the קהל. The עמוני convert has that same feature, so his daughter should be disqualified too.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'appearance'; here it means the special feature of a case.
The common denominator, the feature two sources share.
The majority of the Jewish people; a man 'not in רוב קהל' has marriage rules different from most Jews.

steps.whatToRemember: A הצד השוה joins two sources whose weak points cancel each other out, and then applies their shared feature to a new case.

phrases.english: The feature of this case is not like the feature of that case,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the כהן גדול with an אלמנה, and 'that' is the חלל, from the last few steps.

phrases.english: and the feature of that case is not like the feature of this case.
The common feature between them:
that he is not like the majority of the congregation,
and his daughter is disqualified.
So too here, since he is not like the majority of the congregation,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the עמוני convert.

phrases.english: his daughter is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה, וְלֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה. הַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 19 showed the two sources cover each other's weak points. This step turns that into a single combined proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the daughter of an עמוני convert is disqualified from כהונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared feature of the כהן גדול who married an אלמנה and the חלל: each is 'not like most of the קהל', and each one's daughter is disqualified.

steps.title: Both sources share an element of sin
steps.stepSummary: The combined proof is attacked. The two sources share something else too: each has an element of sin. The כהן גדול's union is a sin, and the חלל was born from a sin. The עמוני convert who marries an עמונית convert has no sin at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the common feature between them? It is that they both have an element of sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the הצד השוה by pointing to a second shared feature, sin, that the עמוני case may not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה only works if the shared feature is the real reason for the law. Here both sources also share sin, which might be the real cause of the daughter's disqualification. If the עמוני convert married an עמונית convert, there is no sin, so the proof does not reach him.

keyTerms.meaning: An element of sin connected to the case.
'Since indeed', which brings in the special feature that weakens the comparison.

steps.confusionAlert: The sin is not the same in both cases. The כהן גדול himself sins by marrying, while the חלל did no sin himself but was born from a sinful union. Both still count as 'an element of sin'.

phrases.english: What about the common feature between them?
For they both have an element of sin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks the combined proof from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה proof that the daughter of an עמוני convert is disqualified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources also share an element of sin, which may be the true cause of the disqualification. A union of an עמוני convert with an עמונית convert has no sin.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was speaking about an עמוני who married a born-Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוחנן's ruling 'his daughter is כשרה' was about an עמוני convert who married a בת ישראל. That union is sinful, and still the daughter is fit. The one being asked confirms: yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you are certainly speaking of an עמוני who married a Jewish-born woman, and you mean that even though his union is a sin, his daughter is fit? He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies which case רבי יוחנן's ruling was about, and the answer confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 showed that the derivation from the כהן גדול and the חלל reaches only cases with sin, so for an עמוני convert who married a convert, רבי יוחנן's ruling would be obvious according to רבי יוסי. רבא בר עולא therefore suggests that רבי יוחנן meant a sinful union with a בת ישראל, where we might have disqualified the daughter. Ruling her fit there is a real new teaching, and עולא confirms it.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman born Jewish, not a convert.

phrases.english: Perhaps, certainly,
you are speaking of an Ammonite who married a Jewish-born woman,
that even though his union is a sin,
his daughter is fit!
He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא וַדַּאי בְּעַמּוֹנִי שֶׁנָּשָׂא בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 21 shows the derivation only works where there is sin, this step answers step 13's 'פשיטא'. רבי יוחנן was speaking about a sinful union with a בת ישראל, where his ruling of 'fit' is a real new teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the original ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי יוסי, רבי יוחנן's ruling seems obvious (step 13), because without a sin the derivation from the כהן גדול and the חלל does not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's case is an עמוני who married a בת ישראל. The union is a sin, and he still holds the daughter is fit.

steps.title: רבין's report of the מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: Support for the 'yes': רבין reported in the name of רבי יוחנן that the daughter of an עמוני convert, or of a second-generation מצרי convert, from a Jewish-born woman is fit according to רבי יוחנן. ריש לקיש says she is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: For when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the daughter of an עמוני convert and the daughter of a second-generation מצרי. רבי יוחנן says she is fit, and ריש לקיש says she is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report from רבין showing that רבי יוחנן really ruled 'fit' in this case, and that ריש לקיש disagreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report proves that רבי יוחנן's ruling covers a forbidden union with a Jewish-born woman. It also adds a parallel case, the second-generation מצרי, and shows that ריש לקיש rules the opposite way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For when [he] came', the usual way of bringing a teaching from ארץ ישראל.
An עמוני convert, who may not marry a born-Jewish woman.
A second-generation מצרי convert, who is also not yet allowed to marry into the קהל.
רבי יוחנן's study partner, who often disagrees with him.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says the daughter of a forbidden union of an עמוני or מצרי שני with a Jewish woman is fit. ריש לקיש says she is disqualified.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For when Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The daughter of an Ammonite convert,
and the daughter of a second-generation Egyptian,
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: she is fit,
and Reish Lakish says: she is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This backs up the 'yes' of step 22 with רבין's report.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן's 'כשרה' refers to a forbidden union with a Jewish-born woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's report of the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

steps.title: The reasons behind each side
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says disqualified because he learns it from a כהן גדול who married an אלמנה. The גמרא then begins to give רבי יוחנן's reason for saying fit, and that reason continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says disqualified, because he learns it from a כהן גדול with an אלמנה. רבי יוחנן says fit,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source behind ריש לקיש's view, and then sets up the explanation of רבי יוחנן's view, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש uses the source from step 15: a forbidden union disqualifies the daughter, as with a כהן גדול and an אלמנה. The amud ends just as the גמרא begins to give רבי יוחנן's reason, which comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it, meaning he derives the law from another case.
A widow, whom a כהן גדול may not marry.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says she is disqualified,
because he learns it from a High Priest with a widow.
Rabbi Yoḥanan says she is fit,

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר פְּסוּלָה — דְּיָלֵיף לַהּ מִכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains the reasoning behind the two opinions reported in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש disqualifies the daughter, learning it from a כהן גדול who married an אלמנה. רבי יוחנן rules her fit, and his reason follows.
